PR #71, "Write Claude default settings over the workspace user's at each start" (open, base `main`, branch `claude-default-settings`, author anton-matosov). It makes the image's Claude defaults overwrite `~/.claude/settings.json` on every workspace start. The reason is that `/home/dev` is a volume filled from the image only once (ADR 0012). The PR states the merge danger: users' own edits to that file are lost at the next start.

**Per file**

- `.claude/settings.json`: adds `worktree.baseRef = "fresh"` to this repo's own Claude settings.
- `GLOSSARY.md`: adds the term **Claude default settings**, meaning the user settings the template image gives every workspace user, taking precedence over the user's own. The entry says to avoid "Managed settings" and "baked-in settings".
- `docs/usage/coder-template.md`: adds a bullet saying the defaults (`images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.json`) are written over `~/.claude/settings.json` at every start. It adds that `~/.claude.json` and project settings are untouched.
- `images/coder-template/Dockerfile`: copies the new `claude-default-settings.service` into `/etc/systemd/user/`. It also copies the JSON to `/usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json`.
- `images/coder-template/agent-services.target`: the target now also wants `claude-default-settings.service`.
- `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.json` (new): the defaults themselves.
  - `worktree.baseRef = "fresh"`
  - `model = "opus"` and `permissions.defaultMode = "auto"`
  - a deny list of 11 tools, including the plan-mode and cron tools
  - `autoMemoryEnabled = false`
  - several `disable*` flags
  - `context7` enabled as a plugin
  - env, attribution and `cleanupPeriodDays` settings
- `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service` (new): a oneshot, `PartOf=agent-services.target`, ordered `Before=` `claude-pre-approval.service` and `claude-remote-control.service`. It runs `mkdir -p ~/.claude`, then `cp` of the defaults over `~/.claude/settings.json`. A code comment says `cp` is used so the write goes through a dotfiles symlink and keeps the link.
- `images/coder-template/smoke.sh`: the tests now check the new behaviour.
  - The symlinked-home case no longer expects the user's `model: smoke` to survive. It checks that `enableAllProjectMcpServers` is set, and that the symlink target equals the defaults plus that key, using `jq --slurpfile`. It still checks that the file remains a link.
  - The pre-approval-off case previously asserted that no settings file exists. It now asserts the file has no `enableAllProjectMcpServers` key and is byte-identical (`cmp`) to the defaults. A new `pass` line covers this.

I found no high-signal issues in the changed code.

What I checked:

- **Unit ordering:** `claude-default-settings.service` runs before `claude-pre-approval.service` and `claude-remote-control.service`, so the defaults are written first and pre-approval adds to them. Because the target starts these units with `Wants=`, systemd also orders the target after them, so `systemctl --user start agent-services.target` returns only once the one-shot units have run. The smoke test's checks right after the start rely on that. It is `PartOf=` the target with `RemainAfterExit=yes`, so stopping and starting the target runs the copy again. The smoke test's second start depends on this.
- **Writing through the symlink:** plain `cp` onto an existing symlink writes to the link's target and keeps the link. Pre-approval then edits that same target file, so the link survives.
- **Smoke test jq and shell:**
  - jq compares objects without regard to key order, so `--slurpfile d … 'del(.enableAllProjectMcpServers) == $d[0]'` is correct.
  - The user's `"model": "smoke"` is replaced by `"opus"`, as the test now expects.
  - With both choices off, pre-approval leaves `settings.json` alone, so the `has(...) | not` and `cmp -s` checks hold on a fresh home.
  - The `shellcheck disable=SC2016` comment is warranted.
- **Dockerfile:** the unit file is added to the user-units `COPY`, and the second `COPY` to `/usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json` creates the missing directory itself. The path matches the one used in the unit and in `smoke.sh`.

Two things I did not count as issues:

- **Broken symlink:** GNU `cp` refuses to write through a symlink whose target doesn't exist. If a user's `~/.claude/settings.json` points at a missing file, the unit fails, whereas `claude-pre-approval` (which resolves the link first) would create the file. That depends on how the user's home is set up.
- **Wording in ADR 0016:** the header comment in `images/coder-template/claude-pre-approval` (unchanged by this PR) says "nothing is ever revoked". In practice the workspace-wide `enableAllProjectMcpServers` approval is now dropped at the next start once trust is switched off, because the defaults overwrite the file. That follows from the intended overwrite, but the ADR 0016 wording may be worth a look.

**Dismissed findings to log (per AGENTS.md):** the two above, both dismissed by me. One depends on the user's setup; the other follows from the overwrite the PR intends.
